items.title: US AI Task Force to Report on Technology’s Risks, WSJ Says
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: <article>A new White House task force will produce a report assessing risks posed by artificial intelligence and what responsibility the US federal government should have over the technology.</article>

items.title: Bessent Says AI Industry Must Own Its Risks and Find Solutions
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: <article>US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized prominent artificial-intelligence figures’ warnings about existential risks posed by the technology as alarmist and unhelpful, calling on the industry to police itself and produce solutions.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Employee Quits With Call for Nuclear-Level Safeguards
items.author: Seth Fiegerman
items.content: <article>An OpenAI employee focused on AI safety has quit the company and warned that top artificial intelligence firms aren’t doing enough to mitigate the technology’s risks, joining a growing chorus of employees raising alarms from within the industry.</article>

items.title: War, Cyber Attack May Spark Next Financial Crisis, RBI Says
items.author: Anup Roy, Siddhartha Singh and Saikat Das
items.content: <article>The next financial crisis could originate from a source outside the world of finance, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said Saturday.</article>

items.title: Taiwan Foreign Minister to Visit Arizona to Deepen Economic Ties
items.author: Yian Lee
items.content: <article>Taiwan’s foreign minister is set to visit Arizona for meetings with local officials and semiconductor companies, underscoring Taipei’s effort to deepen economic ties with the US as President Donald Trump seeks to stabilize relations with China.</article>

items.title: US Hackers Face $1,000 Monthly Pay Cut in Controversial Plan
items.author: Patrick Howell O'Neill and Jake Bleiberg
items.content: <article>US soldiers tasked with hacking American adversaries and defending the nation’s computers are set to see their incentive pay cut by as much as $12,000 a year as part of an overhaul that’s drawn ire from the ranks, according to documents reviewed by Bloomberg and people familiar with the situation.</article>
